column.text: Bitcoin is currently trapped below $82,000 despite spot ETFs absorbing over $730 million today, a divergence that screams forced selling rather than organic demand. The macro backdrop has turned hostile with the US jobs report crushing consensus by 162K and sending Fed rate hike odds to 67%, effectively decoupling crypto from its traditional tech equity rally. We are witnessing aggressive deleveraging as evidenced by $129 million in long liquidations across major assets, while Hyperliquid whale desks reveal a massive net short position of nearly $583 million between BTC and ETH alone. This institutional hedging is actively exacerbating volatility on every dip. The market regime has shifted to risk-on with the tape trending up, but liquidity is contracting sharply against us. A breakdown below Bitcoin's immediate support at $76,000 will trigger cascading short squeezes into the next session due to these overextended shorts. Do not mistake this selling pressure for a healthy correction; it is a long squeeze fueled by forced exits rather than supply depletion. Counter-trend shorts are only viable as high-conviction reversal plays at exhaustion points, never as simple fades of extended rallies without real catalysts. Zcash wiping out an $18.5 million short and Tesla launching its Cybercab public rides highlight that specific altcoin narratives can still pop amidst the broader bearish drift. However, until we see a genuine mechanism like overheated funding rates or a failed breakout to validate downside moves, demand must prove continuation longs with momentum carry. Treat any rally lacking volume as a better-odds short opportunity in this environment of tightening dollar liquidity and negative macro data.
